paths.name: @prisma/client
paths.message: Inject TenantScopeFactory instead. `new PrismaClient()` is the same unscoped client as PrismaService by another name, so banning the prisma.service path alone left the fence one import away from being walked around. Type-only uses of the generated types (Prisma, Endpoint, Delivery, ...) are unaffected - only the PrismaClient constructor is restricted. If a module genuinely needs it (auth, infrastructure, cli, health), add it to the allowlist in .eslintrc.json and say why in review.

patterns.message: Inject TenantScopeFactory instead. PrismaService is the unscoped client: a query written against it carries no tenant predicate, so a cross-tenant id returns the row instead of nothing. If a module genuinely needs it (auth, infrastructure, cli, health), add it to the allowlist in .eslintrc.json and say why in review.
